title: Ko Kyung-pyo apologizes after drunk driving crash and admits wrongdoing
text:
Ko Kyung-pyo apologizes after drunk driving crash and admits wrongdoing - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 11월 14일(토) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Entertainment Ko Kyung-pyo apologizes after drunk driving crash and admits wrongdoing 
 입력 2026.11.14. 10:10 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 Actor 고경표's side apologized over a drunk-driving traffic accident.
 Ko Kyung-pyo's agency, CLN Company, said on the 14th, "First, we deeply apologize to those harmed by Ko Kyung-pyo's drunk-driving accident. We also sincerely apologize for the disappointment and concern caused to everyone who trusted and supported him."
 The agency said, "Ko Kyung-pyo caused a collision with a street-cleaning truck this dawn while driving under the influence, and the breathalyzer confirmed a blood alcohol level that meets the threshold for license cancellation," adding, "Ko Kyung-pyo completed police questioning and returned home, and he admits his wrongdoing and is deeply reflecting on it."
 They added, "We take the severity of drunk driving very seriously, and we will humbly accept any penalties imposed and fulfill our responsibilities, including compensating for the damage."
 The agency also said, "We take this matter seriously as a company and will pay closer attention to managing our actors so this does not happen again. Once more, we bow our heads and apologize to those harmed by this accident and to everyone."
 According to a Yonhap News report that day, Ko Kyung-pyo struck a street-cleaning truck around 3:30 a.m. in the Donggyo-dong area of Mapo District, Seoul, while driving his car. At the time, his blood alcohol level was reported to be at a level that would lead to license cancellation.
 Meanwhile, Ko Kyung-pyo is currently appearing on tvN's "Sixth Sense: B-side" and MBC's variety show "Hangout With Yoo," and he was scheduled to appear in tvN's "The Village Barber" first broadcast Nov. 29 and in the TVING original "The Great Escape: Urban Ghost Stories," which was set to premiere Dec. 2.
 The following is the agency's full statement.
 Hello. This is CLN Company.
 First, we deeply apologize to those harmed by Ko Kyung-pyo's drunk-driving accident. We also sincerely apologize for the disappointment and concern caused to everyone who trusted and supported him.
 This dawn, while driving under the influence, Ko Kyung-pyo collided with a street-cleaning truck, and the breathalyzer confirmed a blood alcohol level that meets the threshold for license cancellation. He completed police questioning and returned home, and he admits his wrongdoing and is deeply reflecting on it.
 We take the severity of drunk driving very seriously, and we will humbly accept any penalties imposed and fulfill our responsibilities, including compensating for the damage.
 We also take this matter seriously as a company and will pay closer attention to managing our actors so this does not happen again.
 Once more, we bow our heads and apologize to those harmed by this accident and to everyone.
